study_characteristics.title: Hypothermic Machine Perfusion in Liver Transplantation — A Randomized Trial
study_characteristics.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine

perfusion_settings.perfusate_type: Belzer machine-perfusion solution (Bridge to Life) supplemented with 3 mmol of glutathione per liter

time_metrics.perfusion_initiation: End-ischemic (after transportation to the transplantation center)

ead.definition: Olthoff criteria (bilirubin >= 10 mg/dL on day 7, INR >= 1.6 on day 7, or ALT/AST > 2000 U/L within first 7 days)

nas.definition: Symptomatic nonanastomotic biliary strictures diagnosed by cholangiography + clinical symptoms/cholestatic labs

tbc.source_location: Table 2 (calculated from NAS 5, AS 23 vs NAS 14, AS 22)

prs.definition: Decrease of >30% in MAP within 10 mins after reperfusion

graft_survival_1yr.source_location: Results section (mentions no difference at 1 year, data in Fig. S3)

patient_survival_1yr.source_location: Results section (mentions no difference at 1 year, data in Fig. S3)

unclear_items_for_review: ACR is reported as 'Rejection of transplanted liver' in Table 4 but percentages are based on total adverse events, not patients.
1-year survival data is mentioned as having no difference but the actual percentages/HR are in the supplementary appendix (Fig S3).
extraction_notes.general_notes: This is the landmark DHOPE-DCD trial comparing end-ischemic dual hypothermic oxygenated machine perfusion with static cold storage in DCD liver transplantation.

d1_randomization.rationale: The study used a centralized, computer-generated randomization process with balanced blocks of six. Allocation was stratified by trial center and primary indication. Randomization occurred only after the liver was accepted for transplantation, ensuring concealment until the point of intervention.
support_quotes: Centralized balanced-block randomization (in blocks of six) was computer-generated, with stratification according to trial center and primary sclerosing cholangitis as an indication for transplantation (yes or no).
Randomization took place immediately after a donor liver had been deemed to be suitable and had been accepted by the transplantation surgeon for a recipient.

d2_deviations.rationale: Patients and organ-procurement teams were blinded. While the surgical and medical teams could not be blinded to the use of a perfusion machine, the primary outcome was assessed by blinded radiologists. There is no evidence of significant deviations from the intended interventions.
support_quotes: Patients and the organ-procurement teams were unaware of the trial-group assignments.
The trial did not interfere with the regular process of organ allocation or acceptance.

d3_missing_data.rationale: A total of 160 patients were randomized, and 156 were included in the final analysis. The four exclusions occurred after randomization but before any trial procedures started (due to liver quality or intraoperative findings), and the reasons were balanced or clinically justified. Data for the primary outcome appears complete for the analyzed participants.
support_quotes: A total of 160 patients were enrolled, of whom 78 received a machine-perfused liver and 78 received a liver after static cold storage only (4 patients did not receive a liver in this trial).
This resulted in the inclusion of 78 patients in the machine-perfusion group and 78 patients in the control group.

d4_measurement.rationale: The primary outcome (nonanastomotic biliary strictures) was defined by prespecified clinical and radiological criteria. Crucially, all cholangiographies were reviewed by two independent radiologists who were blinded to the treatment group and clinical symptoms.
support_quotes: All the cholangiographies, both in patients who were symptomatic and in those who were asymptomatic, were reviewed by two independent radiologists who were unaware of the preservation method and clinical symptoms.

d5_selection.rationale: The trial followed a prespecified protocol and statistical analysis plan that was finalized before the database was locked. The primary and secondary outcomes reported match those described in the methods section and the previously published protocol.
support_quotes: All end-point analyses were prespecified in the protocol and statistical analysis plan, which was finalized before the database was locked.
The trial protocol, which is available with the full text of this article at NEJM.org, has been published previously.

rob_information.overall_rationale: The study was well-conducted with a robust randomization process, clear allocation concealment, and blinded assessment of the primary outcome by independent radiologists. Missing data was minimal and well-explained, and the analysis followed a prespecified plan.
